book.summary: Joe Pass Guitar Chords is a two-chapter practical reference organized as a vocabulary-then-application curriculum. Chapter 1 presents Pass's complete working voicing inventory as a silent catalog of fretboard diagrams across six chord-sound categories — Seventh, Augmented, Minor, Diminished, Minor Seventh Flat Fifth, and Major/Dominant Alteration forms — with pitch labels beneath each diagram and no prose instruction. Chapter 2 immediately deploys that catalog in seven distinct harmonic contexts, embedding the governing principles of tritone substitution, diminished-as-7b9-substitute, augmented chromatic approach, and common-tone lead-note sustain within notated passages the player must read, finger, and internalize. Two explicit prescriptions frame the entire work: chord-symbol qualifier order equals ascending voice order (D7+9+5 means D7 with raised ninth next and raised fifth on top), and lead notes common to successive chords must be sustained across the change. The method is inductive and mimetic — master shapes silently, then watch them move through functional harmonic situations.
key_phrases: symbol qualifier order equals voice order

chapter.title: CHORD FORMS
chapter.summary: Chapter 1 presents Pass's complete working voicing inventory as a silent catalog of fretboard diagrams across six chord-sound categories: Seventh, Augmented, Minor, Diminished, Minor Seventh Flat Fifth, and implied Major/Dominant Alteration forms. Each voicing is rendered as a fretboard diagram with bottom-to-top pitch labels printed beneath; no prose instruction accompanies them. The pedagogical move is presentation-by-catalog — Pass treats the chord shapes themselves as the lesson, expecting the student to absorb voicing vocabulary through silent inspection and finger-pattern memorization.

sections.title: Seventh Chord Forms
sections.summary: Pass presents dominant and major seventh voicings as a complete grid catalog, functioning as the primary origin and resolution target of cycle progressions and turnarounds. No prose accompanies the diagrams; the shapes themselves are the instruction.

engine_rules.name: Seventh Forms as Cycle Origin and Target
engine_rules.preference: default to catalog seventh form at each cycle node
engine_rules.anchor: Seventh Chord Forms

paragraphs.summary: Seventh chord voicings are presented as a silent diagram catalog; students absorb shapes through visual inspection and physical memorization without verbal explanation.

sections.title: Augmented Chord Forms
sections.summary: Augmented voicings are cataloged as chromatic approach chords whose function is to connect by half-step into cycle cadences.

engine_rules.name: Augmented Form as Chromatic Approach Vehicle
engine_rules.preference: sustain augmented color across multiple beats before resolving
engine_rules.falsifier: augmented chord used as tonic with no subsequent cycle resolution
engine_rules.anchor: Augmented Chord Forms

paragraphs.summary: Augmented chord forms are cataloged without prose; their role as chromatic approach chords resolving into cycle cadences is established by the diagram inventory itself.

sections.title: Minor Chord Forms
sections.summary: Minor triad and minor seventh voicings are presented as a catalog serving both ii-chord function in ii-V-I progressions and harmonic color in minor-key passages.

engine_rules.name: Minor Form as ii-Chord in ii-V-I
engine_rules.preference: use catalog minor form at ii position before chromatic approach to V
engine_rules.falsifier: minor form used at tonic position in major key
engine_rules.anchor: Minor Chord Forms

paragraphs.summary: Minor chord forms catalog both triad and seventh voicings; function as ii chords and provide harmonic color in minor-key contexts.

sections.title: Diminished Chord Forms
sections.summary: Fully diminished voicings are cataloged as mobile approach chords with multiple resolution targets, interchangeable with dominant 7b9 sounds.

engine_rules.name: Diminished Form as Mobile Approach Chord
engine_rules.preference: treat diminished voicing as approach rather than destination
engine_rules.falsifier: diminished chord used as stable tonic with no subsequent resolution
engine_rules.anchor: Diminished Chord Forms

paragraphs.summary: Diminished chord forms are mobile approach chords; the catalog provides the full inventory of shapes that may substitute for or approach dominant 7b9 targets.

sections.title: Minor Seventh Flat Fifth Chord Forms
sections.summary: Half-diminished voicings are cataloged as the iio chord in minor iio-V7b9 cadences, resolving to dominant and augmented forms.

engine_rules.name: Half-Diminished Form as iio in Minor Cadence
engine_rules.preference: resolve half-diminished to dominant 7b9 then to augmented
engine_rules.falsifier: half-diminished form used at tonic position
engine_rules.anchor: Minor Seventh Flat Fifth Chord Forms

paragraphs.summary: Minor seventh flat fifth (half-diminished) forms function as iio in minor iio-V7b9 cadences; the catalog provides the voicing shapes for this characteristic resolution path.

chapter.title: CHORD PASSAGES
chapter.summary: Chapter 2 deploys the Chapter 1 voicing catalog in seven distinct harmonic contexts — major-sound resolution via tritone substitution, minor seventh to seventh motion with chromatic approach, seventh-chord substitute turnarounds and cycle progressions, diminished chords as interchangeable approach chords with multiple resolution paths, diminished chords substituting for 7b9 sonorities, augmented sounds resolving chromatically into cycle cadences, and half-diminished to dominant and augmented resolutions. Two explicit prescriptions govern performance: chord-symbol qualifier order equals ascending voice order, and lead notes common to successive chords must be sustained.
key_phrases: symbol qualifier order equals voice order

sections.title: Major Sounds Resolution
sections.summary: The major-sound passage demonstrates tritone substitution as the default dominant-to-tonic resolution device: G13b5 (equivalently Db7+9b5) resolves to Cma9, establishing the tritone sub as a standard approach to major-sound tonics.

engine_rules.name: Tritone Substitute for Major-Sound Resolution
engine_rules.preference: prefer tritone sub (bII7) over direct V7 when resolving to major tonic
engine_rules.falsifier: tritone sub used in context where resolution target is minor or non-tonic
engine_rules.anchor: G13b5 (or Db7+9b5) which re-solves into Cma9

engine_rules.name: Cma9 as Major-Sound Tonic Resolution Target
engine_rules.preference: add ninth to major tonic voicing when arriving via tritone sub
engine_rules.falsifier: plain major triad used as tonic after tritone sub resolution
engine_rules.anchor: G13b5 (or Db7+9b5) which re-solves into Cma9

paragraphs.summary: The first four chords establish movement in C; the fifth chord is a tritone substitute (G13b5 = Db7+9b5) resolving to Cma9.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor: G13b5 (or Db7+9b5) which re-solves into Cma9

engine_rules.name: Db7 as Tritone Substitute for G7
engine_rules.preference: use Db7+9b5 voicing shape when substituting for G13
engine_rules.falsifier: G7 used directly without tritone sub option in major resolution passage
engine_rules.anchor: G13b5 (or Db7+9b5) which re-solves into Cma9

sections.title: Minor Seventh to Seventh Movement
sections.summary: The minor-seventh-to-seventh passage establishes the ii-V movement with Ab13 as a chromatic approach chord between Dm7 and G13.

engine_rules.name: Chromatic Approach Chord Between ii and V
engine_rules.preference: insert chromatic dominant (bVI13) between ii and V for smooth bass descent
engine_rules.falsifier: direct ii-V motion with no chromatic approach chord
engine_rules.anchor: movement in Dm7, resolving into Abl13 to G13

engine_rules.name: Bass Descends by Half-Step into Dominant
engine_rules.preference: use bVI13 voicing whose root is a half-step above the V root
engine_rules.falsifier: approach chord a whole step or tritone away from V root
engine_rules.anchor: resolving into Abl13 to G13

paragraphs.summary: Four chords illustrate movement in Dm7 resolving through Ab13 to G13.

sections.title: Seventh Chord Substitution Turnaround
sections.summary: The seventh passage introduces a substitute turnaround back to G13 and a cycle-of-fifths seventh movement.

engine_rules.name: Substitute Turnaround Replacing I-VI-II-V
engine_rules.preference: prefer substitute turnaround over standard I-VI-II-V when returning to G13
engine_rules.falsifier: standard I-VI-II-V used when substitute turnaround passage is available
engine_rules.anchor: substitute turn-around back to G13

engine_rules.name: Cycle-of-Fifths as Default Seventh-Chord Traversal
engine_rules.preference: follow cycle of fifths as default armature for connecting seventh-chord members

sections.title: Diminished Chord Resolution Options
sections.summary: Diminished chords are established as freely resolvable approach chords with multiple permissible targets.

engine_rules.name: Diminished Chord Resolves Freely to Multiple Targets
engine_rules.preference: treat destination as open; any resolution target is valid
engine_rules.anchor: Resolve the last chord in this sequence into any chord

engine_rules.name: Diminished Resolution via ii-V-I Path
engine_rules.preference: prefer Dm7-G7-Cma7 resolution path when targeting major tonic
engine_rules.falsifier: diminished chord resolving directly to tonic without ii or V intermediary
engine_rules.anchor: Dm7 — G7 — Cma'7

engine_rules.name: Diminished Resolution via Chromatic Descending Bass Path
engine_rules.preference: prefer chromatic descending bass path (Em7-Eb9-Dm9-Db9) when targeting minor sound
engine_rules.falsifier: non-chromatic bass motion in this resolution path
engine_rules.anchor: Em7 — Eb9 — Dm9 — Db9

paragraphs.summary: The diminished sequence establishes that the final chord may resolve into any target, with two concrete paths given.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor: Resolve the last chord in this sequence into any chord. For example: (1) Dm7 — G7 — Cma'7, or (2) Em7 — Eb9 — Dm9 — Db9

sections.title: Diminished as Flat-Nine Substitute
sections.summary: The diminished passage states the defining substitution rule explicitly: a diminished chord may stand in for any dominant 7b9 chord, anchored to the I-VI-II-V skeleton A7-Dm-G7-C.

engine_rules.name: Diminished Voicing Substitutes for Dominant 7b9
engine_rules.preference: use diminished voicing wherever 7b9 appears; treat as freely interchangeable
engine_rules.falsifier: 7b9 chord that cannot be replaced by its corresponding diminished form
engine_rules.anchor: Use of diminished chords for seventh flat ninth chord movement

engine_rules.name: Diminished 7b9 Substitution Anchored to I-VI-II-V Skeleton
engine_rules.preference: apply diminished-for-7b9 substitution at VI and V positions in the I-VI-II-V pattern
engine_rules.falsifier: diminished substitution outside of recognizable harmonic skeleton
engine_rules.anchor: utilizing the basic pattern of A7 — Dm — G7 —C

paragraphs.summary: The diminished passage states the rule that diminished chords stand in for 7b9 dominant chords, demonstrated through the A7-Dm-G7-C skeleton.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor: Use of diminished chords for seventh flat ninth chord movement, utilizing the basic pattern of A7 — Dm — G7 —C

sections.title: Augmented Chromatic Approach
sections.summary: The augmented passage establishes augmented voicings as sustained color chords resolved chromatically into a cycle cadence (A7-D7-G).

engine_rules.name: Augmented Chord Sustained as Pre-Cadential Color
engine_rules.preference: sustain augmented voicing across multiple chord positions before chromatic resolution
engine_rules.falsifier: augmented chord used as a single passing chord with no sustained color function
engine_rules.anchor: first six chords are basically G aug. Movement is used chromatically to get to the basic cycle

engine_rules.name: Augmented Resolved Chromatically into Cycle Cadence
engine_rules.preference: resolve augmented color via half-step voice leading into the first chord of the cycle
engine_rules.falsifier: augmented chord resolved by leap rather than chromatic motion
engine_rules.anchor: Movement is used chromatically to get to the basic cycle (A7 — D7 —G)

paragraphs.summary: Six augmented chords (G aug) are sustained as a color device; chromatic voice motion then connects them into the cycle cadence A7-D7-G.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor: first six chords are basically G aug. Movement is used chromatically to get to the basic cycle (A7 — D7 —G)

sections.title: Chord Symbol Spelling Convention
sections.summary: Pass states the proprietary notation rule that governs the entire book: the left-to-right order of qualifiers in a chord symbol corresponds directly to the bottom-to-top order of voices in the voicing.

engine_rules.name: Chord Symbol Qualifier Order Equals Ascending Voice Order
engine_rules.falsifier: chord voicing where qualifier order in symbol does not match ascending string order
engine_rules.anchor: order of appearance of notes coincides with the spelling of the chord symbol

engine_rules.name: D7+9+5 Assigns Raised Ninth to Middle Voice, Raised Fifth to Top
engine_rules.preference: place raised ninth in next available voice above D7 core; place raised fifth on top string
engine_rules.falsifier: D7+9+5 voiced with raised fifth below raised ninth
engine_rules.anchor: D7+9+5 means D7 with the raised 9th next, and the raised 5th on top

paragraphs.summary: The notation rule establishes that qualifier order in a chord symbol equals ascending voice order.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor: order of appearance of notes coincides with the spelling of the chord symbol. For example, D7+9+5 means D7 with the raised 9th next, and the raised 5th on top

sections.title: Sustaining Lead Notes Between Chords
sections.summary: Pass prescribes that when a top-voice (lead) note is common to two successive chords, it must be sustained across the change rather than rearticulated.

engine_rules.name: Sustain Common Top-Voice Note Across Chord Change
engine_rules.preference: always sustain rather than rearticulate a top-voice note that is common to both chords
engine_rules.falsifier: rearticulation of common top-voice note between C9 and F13
engine_rules.anchor: Try to sustain lead notes from one chord to the next. For example, C9 to F13, sustain the G on top

engine_rules.name: G Sustained on Top Across C9 to F13
engine_rules.preference: use voicing shapes for C9 and F13 that share G on the same top string
engine_rules.falsifier: C9 and F13 voiced without G on top
engine_rules.anchor: C9 to F13, sustain the G on top

paragraphs.summary: The NOTE instructs the player to sustain lead notes common to successive chords; C9 to F13 sustaining G on top is the canonical example.
paragraphs.verbatim_anchor: Try to sustain lead notes from one chord to the next. For example, C9 to F13, sustain the G on top
